boundary_atlas.convexity_wall: abs(epsilon)=1 is excluded because the navigation indicatrix ceases to be strongly convex globally
boundary_atlas.outside_wall: abs(epsilon)>1 is not a Randers metric on all of S2
boundary_atlas.rational_wind: reduced p/q gives global return at 2*pi*q, without claiming this is every least period
boundary_atlas.wind_sign: epsilon maps to -epsilon by longitude reflection and swaps the two oriented equators
boundary_atlas.zero_wind: epsilon=0 gives the reversible round Zoll sphere and a continuum of period-2*pi great circles

collision_boundary.C242: irrational ellipsoid Reeb flow has two simple Reeb orbits but is not a Randers geodesic flow
collision_boundary.C289: charged spherical magnetic flow uses a Lorentz force rather than Zermelo navigation
collision_boundary.C305: constant-wind Euclidean navigation is a control-value problem without compact closed-geodesic classification
collision_boundary.C313: the round sphere is a reversible clean Zoll family, not an irrational two-orbit Randers metric
collision_boundary.C331: Dirac-monopole magnetic dynamics and bundle spectrum are not Katok navigation

model.background: unit round S2 with sectional curvature one and longitude period 2*pi
model.navigation_rule: gamma_F(t)=Phi_t^W(rho(t)) for every unit round great circle rho
model.orientation: oriented Randers geodesics; the metric is nonreversible when epsilon is nonzero

nonclaims: no rational prime or prime-power owner is assigned
no target Euler factor, root number, automorphy, divisor, or functional equation is claimed
no target zero match or Hilbert-Polya operator is claimed
the Poincare determinant is source-local and is not a target Fredholm determinant
finite rational rows do not prove the irrational all-period classification

references.author: W. Ziller
references.role: geometry and closed-geodesic owner for Katok examples

references.author: D. Bao, C. Robles, and Z. Shen

theorem_contract.boundaries: epsilon=0 is round Zoll; sign reversal swaps orientations; abs(epsilon)=1 loses strong convexity
theorem_contract.curvature: the navigation Randers metric has constant flag curvature one
theorem_contract.exclusion: in SO(3), return means R_z(epsilon*T)=g*R_z(-T)*g^{-1}; the axes e3 and g*e3 are distinct off the equators, so closure forces T=2*pi*m and epsilon*T=2*pi*n, impossible for irrational epsilon
theorem_contract.irrational_ledger: if epsilon is irrational, exactly two oriented prime closed geodesics exist
theorem_contract.jacobi: in the canonical transverse Jacobi trivialization P(T) has characteristic polynomial z^2-2*cos(T)*z+1
theorem_contract.nondegeneracy: both irrational-wind equators are nondegenerate because T_plus/(2*pi) and T_minus/(2*pi) are irrational
theorem_contract.rational_face: for reduced epsilon=p/q every non-equatorial geodesic returns by time 2*pi*q; special invariant circles may have shorter least period

universal_symbolic_receipts.rotation_axes: the left rotation has axis e3 and the conjugated right rotation has axis g*e3; these unoriented axes differ exactly off the equatorial frames
